  • Affirms that Québec takes priority over any rule that contradicts it.

Part 4 Constitution Act, 1867
  • Removes the rules on the former Québec Legislative Council, which no longer exists.
  • Replaces the word "legislature" with "Parliament of Québec."
  • Adds three new fundamental characteristics of Québec: state secularism, the model of integration into the Québec nation, and the civil law tradition.

  • Specifies that the Code applies in harmony with the new Québec Constitution.
Part 6 Executive Act
  • Allows the premier to designate a person to hold the position of Officer of Québec.
Part 7 Charter of human rights and freedoms
  • Specifies that rights and freedoms must be interpreted taking into account the collective rights of the Québec nation.

26993:
• This bill simplifies the operating rules of professional orders and gives more powers to the Office des professions du Québec, which oversees these orders.
  • It also allows several health professionals (nurses, midwives, optometrists, dietitians-nutritionists) to perform more acts without prior medical authorization.
Part 1 Professional Code
  • Professional orders will be able to adopt certain regulations without the Office's or the government's approval, if they follow its guidelines.
  • The Office des professions, rather than the government, will now approve codes of ethics and regulations on acts performed by non-members.
  • The Office will now decide which diplomas qualify a person for a permit or a specialist title.
  • The Office will have to create a common rule for all orders on the conciliation and arbitration of professionals' accounts.
  • The Office will be able to create rules that apply to one or more orders at a time, after consulting the orders concerned.
  • The Office, rather than each order, will set the ethics rules for members of the orders' boards of directors, and will be able to investigate and sanction breaches.
  • Orders will have to include more information in their official list of members (the roll), and will be able to add other information by resolution.
  • The minimum number of signatures required to request a special general meeting is changing.
Part 2 Act respecting nurses
  • Nurses will be able to start examinations and tests in more situations, not only in public health.
  • They will also be able to prescribe examinations, medications, substances, products and dressings, according to rules yet to come.
  • The rule that reserved voting rights at general meetings to section delegates only is being removed.
Part 3 Midwives Act
  • Midwives will be able to more easily prescribe and administer contraception and screen for sexually transmitted and blood-borne infections.
  • They will also be able to treat these infections in a person without symptoms whose screening test is positive.
Part 4 Optometry Act
  • Certain restrictions on medications and care that optometrists can offer are being removed.
Part 5 Dietitians-nutritionists
  • Their scope of practice is being expanded, and they will be able to act without needing a medical prescription.
Part 6 Psychotherapy
  • The Interdisciplinary Advisory Council on the Practice of Psychotherapy is ceasing its activities.
  • Marriage and family therapists will be able to practise psychotherapy without a special permit, like psychologists and doctors.
  • The Office will be able to authorize students in training to perform certain psychotherapy acts.
  • The Office will be able to set rules for issuing a psychotherapist permit to people already authorized elsewhere in Canada.
Part 7 Pharmacy Act
  • The government will be able to allow a pharmacist to prescribe or substitute a medication with another one made by a company in which they have a financial interest, under specific conditions.
Part 8 Act respecting prescription drug insurance
  • A new rule will allow a drug manufacturer to provide certain benefits to an intermediary, such as a banner or a chain of pharmacies.
Part 9 Regulation respecting the conditions for recognition of a manufacturer and a wholesaler of medications
  • Manufacturers will also be able to provide these benefits directly to a wholesaler.
Part 10 Act respecting agrologists
  • An act will no longer be considered practice of the profession only if it is done for payment.
Part 11 Several professional acts (agrologists, land surveyors, Bar, notaries, denturology, medical imaging technologists)
  • Adjustments to the internal governance rules of the orders.
Part 12 Charter of the French Language and Act respecting legal aid
  • Consequential amendments related to the changes above.
